root_cause: Postings::by_identity and Postings::by_vid (crates/tgms-engine-core/src/store.rs) are append-only identity indexes with no prune at all, unlike open_rows, which at least prunes per-lookup in read.rs::locate_open. Periodic compaction (compact.rs::compact) physically reseals every row that still exists -- open and closed, since compaction never drops one -- into fresh segments every cycle, and the next lookup (read.rs::index_segments, reached through any correction's close_version -> locate_vid) re-indexes them there, stacking on top of every earlier cycle's now-unreachable entries that nothing ever freed: entries for a superseded cycle's segments become permanently unreachable (their segment id is gone from the current file map, so locate/locate_vid/locate_open silently skip them) but were never removed from the maps themselves. This is the shared engine commit/compaction path (gc() -> evict_segments_not_in), not something specific to the replay reader: reproduced directly with a plain correction + compact()/gc() write loop (no replay involved) showing the same non-plateauing per-commit growth, and confirmed precisely via a new NativeStore::postings_stats() counter (2,190 by_identity/by_vid entries for 400 versions ever committed over 10 compaction cycles, unfixed, against a floor of ~400 fixed).

symptom: a read-only opener raised StateError("event log .../eventlog.jsonl record at offset 4076 has no terminating newline and is not the log's last record -- the replay cursor may not be on a record boundary") from tgms/storage/eventlog.py:270-275, inside EventLog.batches_from's torn-tail tolerance check.
root_cause: Distinct from D-086-reader-torn-tail-race (the JSONDecodeError-shaped race, where tolerance was correctly refused because a required gate did not hold). Here the gate's own inputs are stale: batches_from captures `raw`/`end` when it first meets a torn (non-newline-terminated) record, then re-stats the file with a fresh `size = f.seek(0, 2)` to decide whether that record is still the log's last (eventlog.py:258-259). EventLog.append's write-ahead guarantee is one write() then fsync() then return; if that single append -- completing the SAME record the reader is looking at -- lands between the reader's initial read and its size re-stat, the file has grown past the reader's stale `end`, `end >= size` now reads False, the `writer_active()` probe (the one call site D-086-reader-torn-tail-race's two-gate rule relies on) is skipped entirely, and a record that is now complete and sound on disk is reported as damage. The bug is staleness of the comparison inputs, not a missing gate: re-reading the record at its start offset before deciding 'not last' would show it is now whole.
regression_test: tests/test_reader_torn_tail_race.py::test_writer_completing_the_torn_record_between_read_and_size_check_is_not_damage (deterministic repro via a monkeypatched EventLog.batches_from that completes the torn record on disk at the exact f.seek(0, 2) call; currently xfail(strict=True) -- documents the open bug, must be updated in the same commit that fixes it). 30x re-run of the CI test on this laptop (PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_concurrency.py -k readers_opening_throughout -q): 0/30 failures -- the live race is rare (D-086-reader-torn-tail-race's own wild observations put it near 1-in-2,100 reader reopens), consistent with a single CI hit on 3.11 only.
fix_summary: EventLog.batches_from now retries once: when a torn/unparseable candidate's stale `end` is behind a freshly re-stat'd `size`, it seeks back to `start` and readline()s the record again before trusting a "not last" verdict. If the fresh read is a complete, newline-terminated, parseable record, it is yielded normally; otherwise the end>=size / writer_active decision is redone with the retry's own fresh end and a fresh size (one retry only, no loop, no sleep).

root_cause: Established 2026-09-19 (docs/design/D088_READER_GENERATION_PINNING_DESIGN_2026-09-19.md). At the measured cadence (compaction every ~24s with gc(keep_last=2), a generation's files fully on disk for only ~48s of every 300s --reader-reopen-every-s window) a reader was exposed ~84% of every window once the store outgrew what its own queries had already mapped -- the steady state, not an edge case. Reproduces ONLY cross-process: a second in-process NativeStore handle is protected for real by gc.rs's process-global PINS table (keyed by canonical store root, incremented at open/repin, decremented at Drop), which is exactly why the original 6h same-process diagnosis (this entry's prior root_cause) came back null -- PINS has no cross-process visibility by design ('There is no cross-process reader registry, deliberately', gc.rs).

symptom: Gate E's "compaction stalls (max reader p99 during a compaction window)" row prints "0.000 ms" in every soak to date, unconditionally, regardless of whether a reader's p99 actually spiked during a compaction. This reads as a clean result (no stall) but is an instrument error, not a measurement: it would print 0.000 even on a soak with a real multi-second stall.
root_cause: Two unrelated clocks compared as one. child_writer appends `t_start`/`t_end` to compactions.jsonl from `time.perf_counter()` (process-local monotonic clock, arbitrary origin -- not epoch, not comparable across processes). Every metrics.jsonl gauge sample, including the query_p99_ms series the stall computation windows against, carries `ts` from `time.time()` (epoch). summarize() (scripts/longevity_run.py, around the old line 1541) built the stall window directly from `c["t_start"] - 60 <= t <= c["t_end"] + 60` where `t` is an epoch timestamp and `c["t_start"]`/`c["t_end"]` are perf_counter values -- perf_counter's origin is an arbitrary point at process start, typically nowhere near the Unix epoch, so the window is either always empty or (on rare epoch/perf_counter coincidence) meaningless. An empty window leaves `compaction_stall_p99` at its initial 0.0, which was then written to the manifest and rendered by longevity_report.py as a plain number -- no error, no flag, indistinguishable from a genuinely stall-free run.
effect: Gate E's compaction-stall row has been silently wrong (always 0.000, never computed) in every soak run to date: Soak 1, Soak 2, the 6h observation run, and the 72h soak in flight when this was found. None of those runs' compactions.jsonl records carry the epoch fields this fix adds, so their existing manifest.json summaries remain frozen at the old (wrong) 0.000 -- only a run using the fixed writer produces a real number or the new "not computable" text.
regression_test: tests/test_longevity_aggregation.py::test_compaction_stall_computed_from_epoch_timestamps (a compaction record with ts_start/ts_end must window the reader p99 series correctly) and ::test_compaction_stall_not_computable_without_epoch_timestamps (a record with only the old t_start/t_end fields must report the row as not computable, never a number)
decision_ref: none yet -- found and fixed in the W2w harness-audit lane (2026-09-18), no D- number assigned by a coordinator
note: Fix is forward-only: compactions.jsonl records written before this commit have no ts_start/ts_end and stay permanently not-computable for their run (summarize() cannot retroactively recover epoch timestamps from a perf_counter value). The already-generated manifest.json files for Soak 1, Soak 2, the 6h run, and the 72h soak-in-progress keep their old (wrong) 0.000 unless/until summarize() is re-run against their raw compactions.jsonl -- which for those old-format logs will now correctly render as "not computable" instead of silently recomputing a fresh (still wrong) 0.000. The writer life index (`life`) was added to the compaction record at the same time, threaded through spawn_writer's cfg dict, since it was a one-line addition available at the same call site and lets a --restart-every run's compaction records be matched back to the writer_progress-<life>.json that produced them.
